stem: Dev compares two planet cards. Planet R is nearer the Sun than planet S. Planet R has a thin atmosphere. Planet S has a thick heat-trapping atmosphere. Planet S looks reddish and planet R looks bluish.

parts.text: Which statement is the best guide to their temperatures?

options.text: Planets farther from the Sun are generally colder, but a thick heat-trapping atmosphere can change that.
Planet R must be hotter than planet S because it is closer to the Sun, regardless of atmosphere.
With atmospheres set aside, planet S should be generally hotter than planet R because it is farther from the Sun.
Planet S is hotter because it looks reddish, and planet R is colder because it looks bluish.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Distance from the Sun sets a general temperature trend, but a planet's atmosphere can trap heat and change that trend.

teacher.key_rationale: Farther planets are generally colder, yet atmosphere can trap heat. Closeness alone does not decide when atmospheres differ. Colour is not a temperature rule here.
